summary: Vasily Seseman was a philosopher who studied at Saint Petersburg State University from 1903 to 1909. He later held positions at Saint Petersburg State University (circa 1915–1919), Vytautas Magnus University (circa 1923–1940), and Vilnius University (circa 1940–1950).

Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD from the University of Bonn in 1930. He worked at Visva-Bharati University, served as a professor at Fergusson College, and was appointed professor at the University of Delhi in 1959.

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied at Deccan College and the University of Mumbai. He served as principal of Morris College and Vidarbha Institute, and was later honorary professor at Nagpur University (1957–1966).

Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow. He held posts at the Government Museum in Mathura, State Museum Lucknow, Archaeological Survey of India, and Banaras Hindu University.

Vasudha Dalmia is a scholar of Indology and history educated at Miranda House, Cologne, JNU, and Heidelberg. She taught at the University of Tübingen, served as a distinguished professor at UC Berkeley (2001–2012), and was a professor at Yale (2013–2014).

Vasudha Narayanan is a religious studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees from the University of Madras, University of Mumbai, and Harvard University. She served as president of the American Academy of Religion and is Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida.

Vatroslav Jagić was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna from 1856 to 1860. He held academic posts at Odesa University (1872–1874), Humboldt University of Berlin (1874–1880), Imperial St. Petersburg University (1880–1886), and the University of Vienna (1886–1908).

Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and computational studies who earned doctorates from Central Sanskrit University and National Sanskrit University. He has held positions at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha, Rajasthan Sanskrit University, and Karnataka Samskrit University.

Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indologist who studied at Sir C. R. Reddy College, Andhra University, and Osmania University. He served as lecturer and associate professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and was a visiting professor at Emory University and Chicago.

Vempati Kutumba Sastry is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Central Sanskrit University from 2003 to 2008 and was president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies from circa 2006 to 2018.

Ven. Dhammapāla is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhante Dhammasakkaro and supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti. He completed his education at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Hong Kong.

Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge from 1986 to 1993. She held positions at St Edmund's College, St Hilda's College, and King's College London before joining Yale University as a professor in 2006.

Verrier Elwin was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Dean Close School and Merton College (circa 1921–1925), and served as the first deputy director of the Anthropological Survey of India from circa 1946 to 1949.

Vesna Wallace is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned her doctorate at UC Berkeley. She held the Numata Chair in Buddhist Studies at Oxford and is a Distinguished University Professor and Department Chair at UC Santa Barbara.

Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who earned a BA from Yale University and a PhD from SOAS University of London. In 1984, he was appointed a distinguished university professor of history at the University of Michigan.

Victor Chan is a Tibetologist who was a graduate student at the University of Chicago. He founded the Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education in 2005 and served as Executive Director of UBC's Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program.

Victor Forte is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at Temple University in 2004. As attested in 2007, he served as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Albright College.

Victor H. Mair is a sinologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Dartmouth, SOAS, and Harvard. He taught as an assistant professor at Harvard before joining the University of Pennsylvania in 1979.

Victor Henry was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Douai (circa 1878–1887), the University of Lille (circa 1887–1888), and was appointed professor of Sanskrit and comparative grammar at the University of Paris in 1888.

Victor Turner was an anthropologist and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from UCL and the University of Manchester. He held academic posts at the University of Manchester, Cornell University, the University of Chicago, and the University of Virginia.
